findings.issue: The skip only keeps a pass from stalling while fewer than BATCH (100) unknown rows are due. Skipped rows keep status PENDING and their next_attempt_at never moves, so they stay due forever. They are also the oldest rows (lowest seq) and the query uses ORDER BY o.seq LIMIT 100, so they take the head of every batch. Once 100 or more distinct aggregates hold an unknown-kind row, every batch is all unknown rows, delivered+dead==0, and the round loop breaks. After that no ORDER_EVENT, RESTORE_STOCK, RELEASE_COUPON etc. is ever delivered: the whole-outbox stall the CTO's condition 1 / ADR 0010 is meant to prevent. This is a realistic rollback case. CLEAR_CART uses one aggregate per user (cart:userId) and retries for about 26 h, so during a cart-service outage there is one pending clear per affected user, and 100 users is easy to reach. Per-aggregate ordering itself is fine: an unknown row only blocks newer rows of its own aggregate, and for CLEAR_CART those are other CLEAR_CART rows of the same user, which is correct. The same loop also logs one ERROR per unknown row on every 2 s pass with no limit.
findings.fix: Keep unknown kinds out of the batch while still respecting them for ordering. Add `AND o.kind = ANY(:known)` (Kind.values() names) to the outer WHERE and leave the NOT EXISTS subquery over all kinds, so an unknown row still blocks newer rows of its own aggregate but never uses a batch slot. Log the unknown rows once per pass as a single ERROR with count and ids (or a capped sample). Another option: push next_attempt_at forward for a skipped row without changing attempts or status. Add a test to OutboxRelayTest that puts BATCH+1 bogus rows on distinct aggregates ahead of a valid row and asserts the valid row is DONE after relay().

findings.issue: AC-9b requires stock, coupon, coins and wallet to be released when a placement fails on an open breaker after the order row exists. This test covers only a coupon redeem failure and a coins redeem failure. No test covers the wallet paths on an open breaker: (a) payments.walletDebit refused by an open payment-service breaker, which should run unwind plus reverseWalletDebitDurable (OrderService.java:368-376), and (b) createPayment refused after a partial wallet debit, which should run unwind with wallet=true, so creditWalletBackBestEffort (OrderService.java:406-409). The existing walletFailureUnwinds test mocks OrderRemote and throws a generic IllegalStateException, so it never exercises the RetryableException translation or the durable wallet credit-back rows. The AC wording explicitly lists wallet, so as written AC-9b is only partly proven.
findings.fix: Add two cases to OrderBreakerCompensationIntegrationTest. (1) Stub payments.walletBalance with enough INR, use useWallet=true, and make doThrow(openBreaker("payment-service")).when(payments).walletDebit(any()). Assert DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, order CANCELLED, a RESTORE_STOCK row, and the durable wallet reversal row in WalletCreditBacks' table for this order. (2) Use a partial wallet balance, let walletDebit succeed, make createPayment throw the open breaker, and assert the order is CANCELLED and the wallet credit-back row is recorded for saved.walletAmount().

findings.issue: racingCartsWithoutAddedAtCreateNoOrder does guard against regressions. If the fail-closed check is removed or moved below validateCoupon, the unstubbed remote.validateCoupon returns null, v.discountAmount() throws an NPE, Future.get throws ExecutionException, and the test goes red. But it goes red for that incidental reason, not on the 503 / 0-orders assertions. If someone later stubs the coupon or wallet in @BeforeEach, the test still fails under the mutation, but only through the never()/count assertions. The single-placement cartWithoutAddedAtIsRefused test is the clean proof of AC-2. The racer test's own red/green record is misleading: its pre-change failure did not show the double-order it claims to prevent.
findings.fix: Call couponAndPartialWalletAvailable() at the start of the racer test. A regression then shows up as both racers placing unguarded orders (the DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE and orderCount()==0 assertions fail), not as an NPE. Re-run the pre-change red check and record the real assertion failure.

findings.issue: AC-8 lists six dependencies: product, cart, user, payment, promotion and inventory. The placement-level fail-fast tests (no host call, under 1 s, 503, no order row) cover only product, cart and user. Payment, promotion and inventory rely on the generic per-host capability tests and on the compensation test's simulated RetryableException, which does not go through a real breaker.
findings.fix: Add one placement-level fail-fast case for each of inventory (reserveStock), promotion (validate) and payment (createPayment) using the realClient/StubHost/trip helpers. For inventory and payment, also assert the order is CANCELLED, not that zero rows exist.

summary: Most of PR-A is correct. The AC-2 fail-closed check is in the right place: cartSnapshot() runs right after the replay lookup and before fetchAddress, draft, coupon validation, wallet, save, or any remote side effect. Buy-now skips it. The WARN names the cart-service contract, and the cart-service contract test pins a non-null addedAt (CTO condition 5). The regression tests for AC-1, AC-3 to AC-7 and AC-9 check the right outcomes (one order, 409 for the loser, each charge exactly once) against the real DB unique index. The breaker tests prove half-open recovery, isolation between hosts, and that 4xx is not counted. Two major issues block approval. (1) Relay tolerance of unknown kinds (CTO condition 1) holds only while fewer than 100 unknown rows are due. The skipped rows stay due and oldest forever and fill the ORDER BY seq LIMIT 100 batch, so once 100 or more distinct users have a pending CLEAR_CART at rollback, the old build stalls the entire outbox, the exact hazard this change was moved into PR-A to remove. Per-aggregate ordering is not the problem: an unknown row only blocks newer rows of its own cart aggregate, which is correct. Batch starvation is. Excluding unknown kinds from the outer select while keeping them in the NOT EXISTS fixes it, and a test with more than BATCH bogus rows would prove it. (2) The AC-9b compensation tests cover only the coupon and coins failure points. Neither wallet path (debit refused by an open payment breaker, or createPayment refused after a partial wallet debit) is tested, although the AC explicitly lists wallet release. The A2 two-racer test does go red if the guard is removed, but only through an incidental NPE. Stub the coupon so the 503 / zero-orders assertions carry the failure. Re-record forge-verify at the head SHA.
